note: Biallelic NOTCH3 variants show divergent phenotypes: biallelic cysteine-involving variants cause adult-onset CADASIL-like stroke/dementia, while biallelic loss-of-function variants present in infancy or childhood with neurodevelopmental impairment.

evidence.text: Biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants lead to early adulthood-onset stroke and dementia within the CADASIL spectrum, whereas biallelic loss-of-function variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with childhood-onset stroke and spasticity.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants presented in infancy (9 to 14 months) with developmental delay, seizures, and cognitive impairment, rather than beginning in the 3rd to 5th decades of life.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both. The disease course was characterized by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes, migraine attacks, and seizures.
